report:
Conclusion: The claim is not supported. The concern began in March 2020 from a French minister’s tweet and a hypothesis that NSAIDs might increase ACE2, but regulators reviewing evidence found no established link between ibuprofen/NSAIDs and catching or worsening COVID-19. WHO said it was not aware of published clinical or population-based data showing NSAIDs worsen COVID-19 outcomes; EMA said there was “no scientific evidence” linking ibuprofen to worsening COVID-19; UK CHM/NHS concluded evidence was insufficient to establish a link and said patients could use paracetamol or ibuprofen for symptoms. Later large observational studies and systematic reviews generally found no increase in COVID-19 death, severity, ventilation, or hospitalization with NSAID/ibuprofen use, though observational designs and confounding limit certainty. Practical advice: use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time, avoid NSAIDs if you have usual contraindications (kidney disease, ulcers/bleeding risk, certain heart disease, pregnancy), and seek medical care for warning symptoms.
